_doc: Project 006 v3 — API Manager policy bundle for the three v3 Process APIs (submit-order, initiate-wire, order-status-webhook). Apply the same 4 policies to each deployed CloudHub app via Anypoint API Manager UI or the platform-api REST. These policies layer on top of the MuleSoft-internal logic; they do not replace HITL (enforced upstream in the mulesoft-api skill) or audit (the Lambda writes IR_Audit_Log__c per v3 steering rule 10).
_finra_context: FINRA 3110 supervision + FINRA 4511 books-and-records. All three APIs are order-entry or order-lifecycle surfaces, so the same perimeter applies. Deeper controls live in Salesforce + the Lambda.
_v3_scope: V3 collapses v2's 6 APIs (submit-order, rebalance-portfolio, initiate-wire, run-kyc-screening, open-account, close-account) down to 3 (submit-order + cancel/modify subpaths, initiate-wire, order-status-webhook). KYC + account lifecycle + rebalance are handled in Salesforce directly — MuleSoft is writes-only.

policies.name: client-id-enforcement
policies._purpose: Every order-entry/wire/webhook request must be attributable to a named Connected App. Unattributed calls are rejected at the edge.

policies.name: rate-limiting
policies._purpose: FINRA 3110 supervision: cap write throughput so a runaway loop in the Lambda cannot DoS the downstream OMS. 60 req/min sits well above HITL-paced volume (~1 trade per 5-10 min per advisor) but catches automation bugs fast. Order-status webhooks get a higher cap (600/min) because bursty fills are normal.

config._override_for_webhook: For order-status-webhook app, override maximumRequests to 600 in API Manager UI.

policies.name: json-threat-protection
policies._purpose: Defense against malformed or oversized payloads crafted to exploit the DataWeave parser. Caps match the RAML contracts: requests are flat (max 5 levels of nesting) and carry no free-text fields beyond short memo strings.

policies.name: ip-allowlist
policies._purpose: Only the mulesoft-actions Lambda's NAT EIP should reach submit-order and initiate-wire. The webhook app is the exception: it receives public callbacks from Alpaca, so its IP allowlist should be configured with Alpaca's documented webhook source ranges (or removed in favor of signature verification).
policies._note: ipExpression is a placeholder. Replace via API Manager. Zero credentials in git.

config._override_for_webhook: For order-status-webhook app, replace with Alpaca webhook source CIDRs OR disable this policy entirely and rely on the shared-secret HMAC signature check inside the Mule flow.
